prompt.alinti: Someone open sourced the Claude Job Hunter that landed him the job with 74,000 stars.
It's called CareerOps and it grades every job post against your real CV before you apply.
So if a job gets under 4 out of 5, Claude tells you to skip it.
And he ran 740 job posts through it, applied to only 68 and landed 12 interviews.
Then for every job worth it, Claude rewrites your CV and even drafts your answers.
But it never presses submit, so you check every word and send it yourself.
For the repo link, comment shortlist.
Paste a job post. Claude checks it's still open, grades it against your real CV out of 5, and tells you to skip anything under 4.0.
Its author ran 740 job posts through it, applied to 68, got 12 interviews and his Head of Applied AI offer. Then he open-sourced it: 74,000+ stars on GitHub.
For the jobs worth it, Claude rewrites your CV for that job and drafts the answer to every application field.
It runs on your own machine inside Claude Code. Setup is one command, then you just chat.
